track: Fact-check: neural and AI routes to photorealism in 2026 (real-time enhancement, neural rendering, world models, AI assets)

checks.claim: DLSS 5 has shipped (3 September 2026, NBA 2K27), runs only on GeForce RTX 50, costs about 40–60% of frame rate, and takes the engine frame plus G-buffers (albedo, normals, depth, motion vectors). Integration is through Streamline or an Unreal plugin.
checks.source: NVIDIA developer blog 'What's New for Game Developers: DLSS 5…' (developer.nvidia.com/blog/…dlss-5-with-3d-guided-neural-rendering…, read through r.jina.ai); Tom's Hardware 'Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 will launch September 3…' and 'We tested DLSS 5 in NBA 2K27…' (5 Sep 2026); Notebookcheck/Digital Foundry summary via search: RTX 5090 128.4→62.7 fps (−51.2%), RTX 5070 −55%; gamegpu: 162→68 fps at 4K (−58%)
checks.correction:
Confirmed: the 3 September launch, RTX 50 only (laptops included), and a heavy cost. Digital Foundry measured 51–55%, and one outlet measured 58%, so '40–60%' should read 'about 50–60%'.

Three corrections:
- **Inputs.** NVIDIA's developer blog says the model uses 'frame color and motion vectors', one frame in and one frame out. It lists no albedo, normal or depth G-buffer inputs. DLSS 5 is therefore closer to a structure-preserving colour restyler than a G-buffer-conditioned renderer, which weakens the report's claim that it respects geometry.
- **Developer access.** The blog offers only 'Sign up to be notified for DLSS updates for developers'. No public DLSS 5 SDK was found, so a Godot integration is not just 'unverified': as of today it is not possible.
- **Cloud.** NVIDIA says GeForce NOW Ultimate streams DLSS 5 from RTX 5080 rigs, and those streams can reach a Mac. That covers only catalogue games, not the owner's Godot build.

checks.claim: REGEN runs at over 20 fps at 960×544 on an RTX 4090 while the same GPU renders UE5. EPE is far slower. Every published model targets driving datasets, and using a diffusion model as teacher increases flicker.
checks.correction:
Correct. For precision:
- The paper's standalone RTX 4090 figures (no TensorRT) are about 31 fps at 960×540, about 25.6 fps at 720p and 11 fps at 1080p. EPE manages 2.58 fps at 960×540 on the same card.
- The targets are Cityscapes, Mapillary and KITTI.
- The README states that a FLUX.2-klein teacher gives 'more frequent instances of temporal instability (e.g., flickering)'.
- ONNX export was added on 9 June 2026.

Scaled to the M2 Air's GPU, which has about 1/28 of an RTX 4090's FP32 throughput, REGEN would run at roughly 1–2 fps (my estimate).

checks.claim: The best measured real-time diffusion on Apple silicon is 22.7 fps at 512×512 on an M3 Ultra. The M2 Air would manage about 2–3 fps, and no image-translation model is measured at 30 fps on an M2.
checks.source: arXiv 2605.16259 (M3 Ultra paper, Tables 2, 9 and 15); MLX-DLSS README (raw.githubusercontent.com/iamwavecut/MLX-DLSS/main/README.md); DLSSMac README and docs/COMPATIBILITY.md (raw.githubusercontent.com/Mappsnet7/DLSSMac/main/…); VideoCardz, 20 Sep 2026
checks.correction:
The M3 Ultra figures are exact: SDXS-512 through Core ML reaches 22.7 fps, and SD-Turbo on MPS takes 95.8 ms. The paper also reports Tiny-SD at 47.1 fps, at lower quality.

'Best measured' is out of date. Unofficial ports of NVIDIA's DLSS 5 neural-rendering model now run on Apple GPUs:
- **MLX-DLSS:** 18.4–20.1 input frames per second at 512×384 on an M2 Max.
- **DLSSMac:** 21.96 fps at 960×600, 14.9 fps at 1280×800 and 9.58 fps at 1728×1080, on an M5 Max using the M5 Neural Accelerators and macOS 27.

Scaling the M2 Max figure to the 8-core M2 (about a quarter of the GPU and memory bandwidth) gives about 4–5 fps at 512×384. That is before Godot draws anything and before the fanless chassis throttles. The report's order of magnitude therefore stands; the evidence is now a near-direct measurement rather than a scaling from an M3 Ultra.

checks.claim: M2 hardware and Metal feature tiers: GPU family Apple8, about 2.9 TFLOPS on the 8-core GPU, 15.8 TOPS Neural Engine. MetalFX temporal upscaling needs Apple7, frame interpolation Apple5, denoised upscaling Apple9; Metal 4 tensors and machine-learning encoding need Apple7.
checks.source: Metal-Feature-Set-Tables.pdf (developer.apple.com), rows 128–131 and 171–172; Apple's M2 press release (10-core GPU 3.6 TFLOPS, so 8-core ≈ 2.9)
checks.correction: The feature tiers match the current PDF exactly. The report leaves out one point: on M1–M4, Metal 4 tensor operations run as ordinary shaders with no Neural Accelerators, which the DLSSMac compatibility notes also state. The Neural Engine is not used by these rendering ports; the M3 Ultra paper found it 6.2× slower than the GPU for a 0.87B-parameter UNet.

checks.claim: Genie 3 runs at 720p and 20–24 fps and stays consistent for minutes; DeepMind says it cannot simulate real places with geographic accuracy. Project Genie needs Google AI Ultra and caps worlds at 60 s. Street View grounding is US-only. World models 'look photographic'.
checks.source: DeepMind's Genie 3 blog (via r.jina.ai): '24 frames per second … consistent for a few minutes … 720p', 'unable to simulate real-world locations with perfect geographic accuracy'; blog.google Project Genie: 'Google AI Ultra subscribers in the U.S. (18+)', 'Limitations in generations to 60 seconds'; TechCrunch, 19 May 2026
checks.correction:
The frame rate, resolution, consistency and 60 s cap are confirmed. WorldRoamBench measured 20 fps at 1280×704.

Two things are overstated or out of date:
- **The limitation is paraphrased too strongly.** DeepMind says 'with *perfect* geographic accuracy'. The conclusion (not faithful to the LiDAR) still holds.
- **Street View is not US-only.** TechCrunch reports it went to some US Ultra users on 19 May and that 'Global Ultra users will gain access over the next few weeks'.

TechCrunch's hands-on also undercuts the 'photographic' claim for the real-place mode: the Street View results were 'impressive and recognizable, but still video game quality rather than photorealistic'.

checks.claim: WorldRoamBench (June 2026) tested more than 10 world models on 600+ cases of 10–60 s, and scene memory fell 37% on average from short to long horizons.
checks.correction:
The 37% figure is real. The latest version reads: 'Memory … mean score falls from 65.41 at Short horizon … to 41.28 at Long horizon, corresponding to 37.0% average decay'.

Two details need correcting:
- The latest version has 1,006 test cases; 600+ was v1.
- The 37% is a mean over all models, including weak open ones. Genie 3 keeps the best long-horizon memory (61.84). The average therefore overstates the decay of the best system.

The conclusion still holds: none is reliable across every dimension, and the tests run for 60 s at most, far short of a 5 km walk.

checks.claim: Cosmos 3 (June 2026, OpenMDW-1.1) includes transfer mode. Its Edge model makes 121 frames at 480p in about 13 s on an H100 and 7 s on a B200, image-to-video only.
checks.correction:
The benchmarks are exact: H100 SXM 13.33 s (vLLM-Omni) or 12.68 s (PyTorch), B200 7.09 s, RTX PRO 6000 21.92 s. The table covers image-to-video only, and a transfer cookbook exists. The licence is OpenMDW-1.1.

The README dates the Cosmos 3 release to May 2026, not June; Cosmos3-Edge followed in July 2026.

Nothing in the repository shows transfer results on dense forest, so the report's 'the result looks photographic' is unverified for this scene.

checks.claim: Lighting measured with tools/lighting_stats.py: Godot is inside or at the edge of the owner's photos on exposure key, sunflecks, blacks and highlight B/R. The gap is structure plus about 3 stops of dynamic range (photos 9.6–11.8, Godot 6.5–8.6) and sky peak (166–244 against 109–132). The photos fail the warm-highlight target (0.69–0.80 against 0.29–0.42).
checks.source: Re-run this session: python3 tools/lighting_stats.py on refphotos/U*_1280.jpg, docs/engine_selection/prototypes/godot/renders/*.jpg and renders/ue58_baseline/*.jpg. Extra percentile check in the scratchpad: p01, p05 and p99 in 8-bit terms. Images viewed: godot_sdfgi.jpg, godot_sdfgi_canopy_sun6.jpg, U01, U12, ue58_i
checks.correction:
Every number reproduces to rounding. The interpretation is over-optimistic, for three reasons.

**1. The Godot sample is one camera.** All four 'Godot' frames are lighting variants of the same view, so the 'range' spans settings, not scenes.

**2. The framing is not comparable.** Godot frames are 7.6–9.0% sky; the photos are 0.05–1.1% sky. Global histogram metrics that overlap under such different compositions are weak evidence of matching lighting. By eye, Godot shows a milky haze veil, a dull grey sky, and broad, soft light patches instead of hard sunflecks, over generic conifers.

**3. The '3 stops' is mostly a measurement artefact.** The photos' 1st-percentile luminance is 0.0–1.0 out of 255, meaning crushed blacks. stops_p01_p99 then saturates against the tool's EPS=1e-4 floor, so it measures black clipping in the photographer's grade, not scene dynamic range. The report blames JPEG noise, which is the wrong mechanism. On the 5th–99th percentile range the gap is about 1–2 stops (photos 7.5–10.5, Godot 6.0–7.3).

The robust differences are brighter highlights (photo p99 114–178 against Godot 87–110 in 8-bit), black level and haze. Much of that is tone curve and grade, not rendering.

The warm-highlight finding is confirmed: photos 0.69–0.80, and U15 0.585, against UE g–j at 0.29–0.42.

checks.claim: Hunyuan3D 2.1's open-weights licence excludes the UK. TRELLIS.2 is MIT-licensed, takes about 60 s per asset at 1536³ on an H100, and needs at least 24 GB of NVIDIA memory.
checks.source: raw.githubusercontent.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2.1/main/LICENSE (Territory excludes EU, UK and South Korea); raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/TRELLIS.2/main/README.md

checks.claim: A rented H100 costs about $3.25 an hour (median, on demand).
checks.correction: The page now shows a current median of $3.38 per GPU-hour on demand, and the cheapest in stock at $1.30. The offline 'photo pass' is cheaper than the report implies if the owner shops around.

checks.claim: Decart Lucy 2.5 costs $0.02 a second at 720p for real-time restyling (about $72 an hour).
checks.source: docs.platform.decart.ai pricing (via r.jina.ai); therundown.ai Lucy 2.5 page
checks.correction:
The price is correct.
- **A cheaper option was missed:** Lucy Restyle 2 does real-time style transfer at $0.01 a second, about $36 an hour.
- **The 1080p claim is Decart's own:** the published price covers 720p only.
- **Decart's terms matter for a public project:** they grant Decart broad rights to use inputs and outputs, and they treat inputs as non-confidential.

omissions: **What DLSS 5 actually uses.** It is conditioned on colour and motion vectors, not on G-buffers, and it has no public developer SDK yet. The report's option (a), an RTX 50 PC plus DLSS 5 in a Godot fork, is currently blocked rather than merely risky.

**Photographic by what standard.** The owner's reference photos carry a strong grade: crushed blacks (p01 of 0–1/255), desaturation and an unknown processing chain. Part of the gap to 'photographic' is therefore closable by grading the tonemapper output, not by rendering. The report should have said that the gate needs ungraded reference photographs of known provenance before any photorealism measurement means much.

**Scene-comparable test frames.** The lighting comparison uses one Godot viewpoint with about 8% sky against photos with about 1% sky. A fair test would render Godot views matched to the photos' framing: horizontal view under a closed canopy, near-zero sky.
**GeForce NOW Ultimate** streams DLSS 5 to Macs, but only for catalogue games. It shows the owner what DLSS 5 looks like, not what it would do to their own world.

**What DLSS 5-class models do to forest.** NVIDIA's demos and the MLX-DLSS or DLSSMac tests use characters, interiors, Witcher 3 and Control. None tests dense forest or thin branching structure. Whether a neural pass would add realism to foliage or smear it is unknown.
overall:
The headline answer survives: no, not on the fanless M2 Air in free roam while staying faithful to the LiDAR. Several supporting details are wrong or out of date, and the most relevant new evidence is missing.

**What I confirmed:**
- **Research numbers** (checked against primary sources):
  - REGEN on an RTX 4090;
  - the M3 Ultra diffusion paper (22.7 fps; 95.8 ms);
  - AlayaRenderer-Flash at 31.54 fps on an H200;
  - Magpie at about 32 fps and 34 GB on an H100;
  - the Cosmos 3 Edge benchmarks.
- **Mac feature and licence facts:** the Metal feature tiers for Apple8, the Hunyuan3D UK exclusion and the TRELLIS.2 details.
- **Pricing:** Lucy 2.5 at $0.02 a second.
- **The lighting numbers:** every figure from tools/lighting_stats.py reproduces exactly.

**What is wrong or out of date:**
- **DLSS 5 inputs:** NVIDIA says colour plus motion vectors, not G-buffers.
- **DLSS 5 access:** there is no public developer SDK, only a notify-me sign-up, so the Godot route is blocked rather than 'unverified'.
- **Street View grounding in Genie** is rolling out to Ultra users globally, not US-only. TechCrunch judged its output 'video game quality rather than photorealistic', which contradicts 'world models look photographic'.
- **WorldRoamBench:** the 37% memory decay is an all-model average (Genie 3 decays least), and the case count is now 1,006.
- **Smaller slips:** Cosmos 3 came out in May, not June; the H100 median is $3.38, with $1.30 available.

**Over-optimism:** the lighting interpretation.
- The Godot 'range' is one camera with about 8% sky, against photos with about 1% sky.
- The '3 stops of dynamic range' gap is mostly a measurement artefact. The photos' crushed blacks (1st percentile at 0–1/255) pin the metric to its EPS floor; the cause is not JPEG noise, as the report says.
- The robust differences are highlight brightness, black level and haze. Much of that is grade and tone curve, which is cheaper to fix than the report implies.
- By eye, the Godot frame still has a grey sky, a haze veil and soft, broad light patches, so 'lighting already overlaps the photos' flatters it.

**Over-pessimism, or a missed opportunity:**
- The unofficial DLSS 5 ports to Apple GPUs (MLX-DLSS and DLSSMac) give near-direct evidence: 18–20 fps at 512×384 on an M2 Max, and 22 fps at 960×600 on an M5 Max.
- That supports the 'not real-time on this Air' verdict, at about 4–5 fps extrapolated. It also shows that an offline local photo pass on the Air, and an M5-class Mac for low-resolution interactive use, are technically possible.
- Both are legally unusable for a public repository, because the weights are extracted from NVIDIA's libraries and are not licensed.
- Ground-captured Gaussian splats or photogrammetry are the one route to genuinely photographic, place-faithful free roam on the M2, for small captured areas only. The report does not consider them.

**Net answer for the owner:** photorealistic free roam across the whole 5 km plot on this Mac is not achievable with any 2026 neural route. Photographic-looking results are achievable in three narrower forms:
- offline clips;
- captured hero areas;
- on different hardware.

The measured lighting gap is smaller in rendering terms, and larger in structure and sky, than the report's framing suggests.
